judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass House Bill 5004, which sets new state targets for cutting greenhouse gases, the gases that cause climate change. It also sets new targets for state agencies, including a goal of using only electricity that gives off no carbon. The law creates a Connecticut Clean Economy Council to advise on climate and clean energy policy. The council must also plan how to move workers out of fossil fuel jobs and into clean energy work. The law adds heat pumps to the projects that qualify for school building grants. The state's energy department must write a plan for making heat pumps affordable in homes, and report that plan to lawmakers. A heat pump heats and cools a building with electricity instead of burning fuel. The state must also post a model policy that towns can choose to use when buying in environmentally sustainable ways. And the law widens what existing open-space land grants can pay for, including turning open space into urban farms. It passed the Connecticut House of Representatives 98-47 and became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass House Bill 6913, which bars nursing homes and assisted living communities, and their staff, from discriminating against the people who live there. The banned grounds include race, religion, sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, marital status, age, and national origin. Each facility must post a notice saying it does not discriminate. Staff who work directly with residents must take training on caring for people from different backgrounds. Facilities must also respect residents' physical privacy during care. If a facility breaks these rules, the state health commissioner can use the same penalties the law already allows when a facility breaks licensing rules. Those include suspending or taking away its license. It passed the Connecticut State Senate 26-10 and became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass House Bill 7042, which lets people sue gun makers, distributors and sellers that fail to set up and enforce reasonable controls over how their products are sold and marketed. Those controls are steps the law requires, such as ones designed to prevent sales to people who are banned from having guns. A person harmed by a violation can sue, and so can a town or the state. The law also bars those businesses from purposely and knowingly advertising in ways that promote illegal sales or use, or an unreasonable public safety risk. Separately, it changes how far back the state looks at certain Connecticut misdemeanor convictions that block someone from getting a handgun permit. That window drops from 20 years to eight years. The law adds some out-of-state misdemeanors to the list of convictions that block a permit. It also says the crime of illegally firing a gun does not cover firing one in lawful self-defense, or to lawfully defend someone else. It passed the Connecticut House of Representatives 100-46 and became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass House Bill 7066, which requires every public school to name an administrator to handle contacts with federal immigration officers. School boards must add steps for those contacts to their school security and safety plans. School staff cannot be punished for following those steps. The same law limits state and town purchases and use of drones built by what it calls covered foreign entities. That includes governments such as China or Russia, people and companies tied to them, and entities on federal restriction lists. It also limits flying drones near sites the law treats as critical infrastructure. With some exceptions, it bars arming an aircraft or drone with a deadly weapon or certain other dangerous devices. The law lets college athletes be paid through endorsement deals and through agreements that share sports revenue with them. The governor later struck out the law's three spending sections. It passed the Connecticut House of Representatives 94-49 and became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass Senate Bill 1, which creates a permanent fund for early childhood education. It orders Access Health CT to study the need for help with health insurance for child care workers. Access Health CT must then set up a program for the 2027 budget year. The law adds money for special education. It creates a grant districts compete for to run their own special education programs, and a grant program for behavioral health support. It creates an education ombudsperson's office, an official who helps families with complaints. The state education department must produce a guide for families on special education. The state must also write a model contract for special education transportation. The law also orders a study of whether minority students are placed in special education more often than they should be. It passed the Connecticut House of Representatives 101-45 and became law.

The law also orders a study of whether minority students are placed in special education more often than they should be. It passed the Connecticut House of Representatives 101-45 and became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass Senate Bill 3, which requires businesses to advertise a price that already includes every fee a customer must pay. Taxes and government fees can still be added on top. Landlords must likewise include recurring fees in the rent they advertise. The law creates a right to repair. Certain makers of electronics and appliances must make repair manuals, parts and tools available on fair and reasonable terms. It also widens the law against price gouging. The law defines that as charging a price during a declared emergency that is unconscionably excessive, or far beyond what is reasonable. Companies must send a yearly reminder about subscriptions that renew on their own, and must let customers cancel easily. It passed the Connecticut House of Representatives 112-34 and became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass Senate Bill 9, which requires insurers who sell home or renters policies to tell customers that flood insurance is available. Mortgage lenders must tell applicants about flood damage risk and flood insurance. It adds flood questions to the form a seller fills out about a home's condition. All new single-family homes now need a coastal review, which checks how building near the shore affects the coast. Starting in October 2027, town plans for evacuation and for reducing disaster damage must address threats from rising sea levels. Towns must also report data on their bridges and culverts, the pipes that carry water under roads. The law also restricts a class of rat poisons called second-generation anticoagulants, and a class of pesticides called neonicotinoids. It passed the Connecticut House of Representatives 115-33 and became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass Senate Bill 1234, which bars libraries that get public money from signing or renewing e-book and digital audiobook deals that prevent, limit or restrict the everyday lending and operating tasks the law lists. The ban does not start right away. It begins 60 days after the secretary of the state decides that one or more other states with at least seven million people combined have passed a substantially similar law. It passed the Connecticut House of Representatives 106-38 and became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass Senate Bill 1328, which bars private parties from owning, running or managing state prisons, community correctional centers and community reintegration centers. Only the Department of Correction commissioner and department staff may hold and supervise the people kept in them. Facilities owned or run by the federal government are not covered. Neither are community programs that offer housing, transportation, jobs and counseling. It passed the Connecticut House of Representatives 109-37 and became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass Senate Bill 1358, which requires state agencies to raise the rates they pay each year on their ongoing contracts with nonprofit human services providers. Starting July 1 2027, the yearly raise matches the past year's rise in the Northeast consumer price index, a measure of inflation. An agency may not cut the rate when that measure falls. The state must also raise Medicaid rates for these providers by the same amount, unless federal Medicaid rules do not allow it. The rule covers providers who serve people with physical, intellectual or developmental disabilities, and providers of behavioral health services. It passed the Connecticut State Senate 28-8 and became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass Senate Bill 1444, which lets towns approve turning commercial buildings into housing through a fast review. That review skips the public hearing and the special zoning approvals such a project would normally need. The town still checks that the site plan follows its zoning rules, and that public health and safety will not be substantially hurt. The owner must certify that the building sat empty, or was less than 50% full on average, for the year before applying. The zoning commission must decide within 65 days. Industrial buildings such as warehouses and factories are not covered. It passed the Connecticut House of Representatives 105-43 and became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass Senate Bill 1542, which bars a police officer from putting handcuffs on a child the officer knows is under 14. The ban runs from the child's first contact with the officer until a court has decided the child broke the law. Handcuffs are still allowed when they are needed for public safety. They are also allowed when the child uses or threatens physical force against the officer, or when a court orders restraints under its existing policy. It passed the Connecticut House of Representatives 99-49 and became law.
